name: Royal Danish Library, LOAR: Veda-recitationer (Kirchheiner collection)
note: Originally 224 cassette tapes covering all four Vedas across six oral traditions, downloadable individually or as zips. This is the master behind the accepted source. It is declined as a *direct* route because its files are cassette-side length and carry no per-stanza boundary; the boundary this artifact relies on is VedaWeb's segmentation of this same master. Recorded because the accepted rows' consent chain terminates at this item - and because the collection's non-Rigvedic holdings, with named Samavedic reciters, are a live lead for the Samavedic and Yajurvedic audio gaps that lies outside this agent's write surface.
recension_claim: Rigveda Samhita; recension not stated at item level
recension_verified_as: not independently verified at this item; the accepted rows' recension is verified on the segmented delivery, per stanza
reciter: D. P. Kinjawadekar for the Rigveda Samhita; the collection as a whole names several reciters, including M. Ittiravi and T. Narayanan Nambudiri for the Samaveda
rights_note: Royal Danish Library item statement, read 2026-09-15: "Copyright protected, but you can use it for non-commercial purposes"; republishing requires a written agreement with the Royal Danish Library; users must credit the author. name: Internet Archive: Rig-veda shakala-samhitA (Rg-veda-shakala-auro1)
note: The only public per-hymn Rigveda recitation found that covers the Valakhilya. Declined for every key because one file is one whole hymn: mapping a 10-stanza hymn file onto a single mantra is exactly what campaign rule 4 forbids, and the item publishes no cue index, chapter mark or timestamp from which a stanza boundary could be derived. The .afpk files beside the audio are Internet Archive audio-fingerprint peaks, not cue sheets. Kept on record as the fallback if the accepted source goes dark, and as an independent structural witness that the Valakhilya belongs inline.
recension_verified_as: consistent with Sakala on structure: 1,028 hymn files with per-mandala counts 191/43/62/58/87/75/104/103/114/191, and 08-049 through 08-059 all present, i.e. the Valakhilya inline. Not verified by text, because the item publishes none.
rights_note: No licenseurl and no rights field in the item metadata; community upload by kashcidv@gmail.com, described only as 'Via aurobindo.ru'. Rights unknown.
snapshot: archive.org/metadata read 2026-09-15: 1,028 .mp3 and 1,028 .ogg, one pair per hymn

name: Internet Archive: Rigveda Parayana - Complete (rig-veda_recitation_202009)
note: Declined for every key: tracks span hymn ranges and their own labels mark the ends as approximate ('partial', 'incomplete'), with no cue index. Its evidentiary value is elsewhere and it is large. Its '(incomplete)' markers fall on M6_S75, M7_S67, M8_S13 and M9_S97, it marks M1_S145 incomplete, and it skips M9_S98 entirely - which together are 66 of the 70 verses VedSearch marks as having no Sanskrit audio. Two independent circulating parayana recordings sharing the same lacunae means those 70 are a gap in the recorded tradition that reaches this product, not a harvesting failure.
recension_verified_as: not verified. Its Mandala 8 track labels run to M8_S92, so it uses the same 1,017-hymn presentation as VedSearch and omits the Valakhilya.
rights_note: No licenseurl and no rights field; community upload by ajayakumara1@gmail.com.
snapshot: archive.org/metadata read 2026-09-15: 54 .mp3 of roughly 44 minutes each, labelled with hymn ranges

name: Internet Archive: Rigveda Chanting (Veda Prasara Samiti)
note: Declined for every key: the tracks carry no hymn or verse label at all, so there is no locator below 'Part NNN' and no candidate mapping for a single stanza could even be formed, let alone verified. ASR could propose one; by campaign rule an ASR proposal never establishes a mapping, so none was run.
recension_verified_as: not verified, and not verifiable here: the item publishes no text and no index. Veda Prasara Samiti masters are the family this project has already recorded as a recension trap for the Yajurveda.
rights_note: The only rights-clean candidate among the declined set, and the least mappable.
